note: FICTIONAL held-out interview. Never used to build the persona or its evidence.

turns.q: Tell me about the last time a new device rolled out on your unit.
turns.a: Last spring we got new pumps. They gave us a short in-service at shift change and the night crew basically got a handout and that was it. I ended up showing two of my night nurses myself at the bedside the first week.

turns.q: What do you do when something on the pump doesn't make sense in the middle of a shift?
turns.a: I try the card I keep with the steps first. If that doesn't clear it, I call biomed. I'm not sitting on hold with the manufacturer with a patient waiting.

turns.q: How do you feel about all the confirmation screens?
turns.a: After the second one that asks the same thing, I'm tapping through. I know I shouldn't, but you stop seeing them.

turns.q: Would a phone app that shows pump status help you?
turns.a: Not really. I've got ten other things buzzing already. What I want is to know that when the pump alarms, it means something.

turns.q: What happens when you float to a different unit?
turns.a: That's when I get careful. Every unit has its pumps set up a little differently and I don't trust my muscle memory there.

turns.q: How involved are you in deciding which pump the hospital buys?
turns.a: Not at all. Purchasing and biomed handle that. I find out when the boxes show up.
